name: notepad
description: Microsoft Notepad (Win11 build). Authored against a real running window: every landmark below came from an actual OCR read of the live client area, not from guesswork. This is the reference profile for a third-party application Frame Forge did not build.

authorized_use.attestation: The owner's own Windows installation, offline, for supervised QA of the automation system itself. No file is ever saved, overwritten, or closed by any shipped scenario.

landmarks.name: tab_title
landmarks.description: The unsaved-document tab. Its presence is how a scenario knows it is pointed at a scratch buffer rather than the user's own open file.

landmarks.name: document_area
landmarks.description: The document body. A colour probe rather than a template: the body is a large uniform field whose exact colour is stable, which is exactly the case a colour probe is good at and a template is not.

landmarks.name: save_prompt
landmarks.pattern: Do you want to save changes
landmarks.description: Notepad's modal 'Do you want to save changes?' dialog. Declared so a scenario can assert it is ABSENT before sending any input - that assertion is what guarantees Frame Forge cannot press Save on the user's behalf.

metadata.landmarks_authored_from: live OCR read of the running window, scripts/probe_notepad.py
metadata.allow_irreversible_note: Granted solely so a QA scenario may type into the document buffer. TypeText is classified C3 (text lands somewhere it cannot be undone by us). No shipped scenario may save, print, or close a document; the relevant intents are in forbidden_intents and no scenario binds Ctrl+S.
metadata.safety_note: Scenarios must target a tab matching 'Untitled'. The tab_title landmark exists so a scenario can assert it is pointed at a scratch buffer, never at the user's own open file.
metadata.identity_note: Identity is the window (class + process), deliberately not the document title. Notepad restores its previous session on launch, so a freshly started instance may open the previously used file rather than a blank document - and a title-anchored target simply never appears. Window identity and document identity are different things, and only the former belongs in a TargetSpec. Which document is active is an assertion, not an identity.
metadata.text_method_note: Declared 'scan' because Notepad's editor is a Win32 EDIT control that reads raw key events. The shared 'ui' preset defaults to 'unicode', which that control ignores - found because the first live run typed nothing at all and the report said so plainly.
